purpose: Explicit game-scaled starting factory allocations for all 197 core OMEGA countries and all 21 canonical factory categories, with traceable allocation confidence.

model.oneUnitMeaning: One abstract starting factory unit in the strategy simulation; it is not a census of a physical factory.
principles: Use the existing 21-type canonical factory catalog.
Every core country gets every factory type key, including explicit zero counts.
Keep industrial specialisation and resource context distinct from raw mineral reserves or current inventory.
Counts are scaled for gameplay and never copied directly from real-world facility totals.
Country counts are a starting baseline; later player construction/upgrades are tracked separately.
Preserve every country existing total starting factory-unit budget when revising category quantities.
Keep each country pre-existing Universal Materials umbrella quantity fixed; it is not a standalone observed establishment class.
Prioritize retained country specialization profiles, and distinguish source-backed specializations from earlier game-modelled profiles.
Use comparable same-year broad-sector observations only for low-confidence macro simulation; never present them as proof of individual factory subsectors.
Do not use unvalidated country resource-context tags as quantitative evidence for factory allocation.
Preserve previous allocations where no comparable macro-sector profile or specific specialization evidence exists.

sectorAlignment.comparisonRule: Compare agriculture, industry and services value-added shares only when at least two numeric observations share the exact same observation year; an all-zero sector set is non-comparable and its raw observations remain preserved.
sectorAlignment.manufacturingRule: Manufacturing value added is a component of industry; its band is compared only when the observation year is within three years of the broad-sector comparison year.
sectorAlignment.archetypeRule: Specific factory-type specializations are preserved. Generic resource-processing labels are refined only from existing explicit game specialization IDs. Countries without a mapped sub-sector specialization receive a cautious broad macro-sector archetype, not an invented factory-type claim.
sectorAlignment.simulationRule: This context informs the game-scaled starting profile; it is not a real-world factory census or an official industry classification.
sectorAlignment.missingRule: Unavailable or non-comparable observations remain null; they are never converted to zero.

factoryAllocationRevision.resourceContextExclusionReason: The retained country resource-context index does not provide sufficiently validated country-specific production quantities or measured reserves for these factory-type allocations, and generic repeated tags were observed. It remains available as a separate legacy context source.

sourcePolicy.primarySpecializations: Existing specializationEvidence sources are retained. Source-backed specializations identify relevant categories, not a physical facility count.
sourcePolicy.macroProfiles: World Bank same-year agriculture/industry/services and manufacturing shares are broad economic indicators. Macro-only rows are low-confidence simulation, not specific subsector evidence.
sourcePolicy.resourceContext: Not applied to V2 quantity weighting until country-specific resource amounts, production and industrial utilization are validated.
sourcePolicy.unavailableValues: Missing, stale or non-comparable observations never become factual zeroes.
